answer: In an agent marketplace that pays for mapping a mesa or surveying an inlet for an atlas, every bidding identity must lock the same refundable bond. Bonds stay locked until the job’s dispute window closes, and a verifiably false submission forfeits the bond. Creating names is cheap, but activating a thousand bidders requires a thousand bonds upfront. Splitting one bankroll across fake identities cannot increase the number of bids it can support.
